what_it_proves: the clevis (outer cheek) takes <= the 0.6 share the joint was sized on (h1_crown.json, BL-051 counterbored heads: strength 3.11, fatigue 1.4; at share 1.0 1.87 / 0.84), the dry, un-preloaded butt joint stays shut at the cradle load, the heads bear on the counterbore floor without pull-in (HEAD-BEAR), and the US2 arm root strain matches the lug model (STAY-STUB, CROWN-SECTION)
gates: frame release R1 (the US2 lug as built from two printed parts)
safety_at_stake: US2 cradle anchor (bag-off / float meat on the frame): joint fatigue 1.4 at share 0.6, 0.84 at 1.0 (h1_crown.json, governing row cradle_lane_b50)
specimen: `designs/pack_5200/print/frame_h1/test_pieces/us_route_stay_R.stl` + `designs/pack_5200/print/frame_h1/us2_clevis_R.stl` (a SECOND print of each: HE-FIT step 0 uses the first) printed with the CA-1 bars and conditioned 7 days. The route piece: frame profile of BUILD_H1.md section 3 with SUPPORTS REQUIRED (it touches the plate over only 9 mm2, BL-053 print_settings_bl053.json): tree supports from the build plate in PAHT-CF, blockers in every bore, pin hole, bolt hole and trap, scars sanded flat (BUILD_H1 section 4), filament about 178 g, about 6.3 h. The clevis: frame profile of BUILD_H1.md section 3, NO supports (it prints flat), blockers in the holes, annealed 90 C 6 h, filament about 14 g, about 0.5 h. Clevis holes reamed 5.1, bolted with 2 Ti gr5 M5 x 35 DIN 7984 with the heads in the printed 9 mm counterbores and NO washer under the head, 2 A2 nuts in the side traps, 2 x 10 mm OD DIN 433 washers on the NUT side only (NOT the z 234 joint's M5 x 45 / 12 mm washers; shopping list), blue threadlocker, snug; check the heads sit below the clevis face (a steel rule across the face does not touch them; design 0.5 mm below) (no preload credited, CLEVIS-DRY); strain gauges (1 mm foil, 120 ohm, cyanoacrylate on the sanded PAHT) on the US2 arm root (R side, bag face, 3 mm off the stay surface, gauge axis along the arm); root stress = strain x 3.86 GPa (youngs_modulus_xy_mpa, record pa12_cf_fdm_paht); TEMPERATURE (BL-054, review 5 m-8): wire each gauge as a HALF bridge with a dummy gauge of the same lot bonded on an unloaded offcut of the same print, lying beside the specimen (it cancels the PAHT-CF's thermal strain); write the room temperature at every reading; with no dummy, re-zero the bridge unloaded at every stop and log the temperature (REQUIRED since BL-052); one sewn US eye (25 mm, necked as op 'US', 18.6 mm slot) on hardened steel M5 x 50 dowel (DIN 6325 m6, HRC 58-62; NOT a 7075 frame pin; it stands about 5 mm proud of each hinge cheek so you can grip it) in the US2 throat with its UHMWPE sleeve
steps: clamp the piece by its stay ends on the lever rig base (as IM3-EC); 1 mm PTFE shim between the eye and the INNER cheek so the eye bears on the OUTER cheek (the clevis: CLEVIS-SHARE worst case); lead the US eye's strap aft and down at 31 deg below the bag direction (the lug check's cradle line; the lane span gives 23.0 deg for US2, which loads the joint less in shear-down) through the rig link; pencil lines across the joint face top and bottom, a 0.05 mm feeler at hand; (1) static: turnbuckle in place of the spring, pull in steps to 720 N (73.4 kg), hold 60 s; at 720 N try the 0.05 mm feeler at the joint face from both sides and both ends; unload, check the pencil lines; (2) cycles: spring back in, R about 0.1 (48 -> 480 N), 1e5 cycles, stop at 1e3, 1e4 and 1e5 to check the feeler at 480 N and the pencil lines; (3) at the end re-check the bolts' torque mark and look at the arm root, the throat floor and each head counterbore (no pull-in, no crack round the head: HEAD-BEAR) with the loupe; STRAIN GAUGE (required, BL-052): read the US2 arm-root gauge at 240 / 480 / 720 N in step (1) and at the peak at each stop in step (2); record strain and root stress (results rows)
pass_fail: no joint opening: the 0.05 mm feeler does not enter the joint face at 720 N or at 480 N at any stop; pencil lines step <= 0.05 mm (none visible under the loupe); no crack at the cheek root, the arm root, round the bolt holes or at the head counterbores, no head pull-in; the bolt torque marks have not moved; 1e5 cycles run out; US2 root stress (gauge) <= the h1_crown lug model's root stress at the same load (structural-fea-engineer reads it off; ASSUMPTION STAY-STUB / CROWN-SECTION)
cost_basis: about 140 g PAHT-CF at USD 80/kg (us_route.json test_piece g_as_assembled) + the clevis bolts on the shopping list
notes: BL-050 B (orchestrator): new. BL-052: M5 x 35, no head washer, 2 nut-side washers (BL-051 counterbore); the US2 root gauge is required. The US test piece printed for HE-FIT step 0 can be re-used AFTER step 0 only if this test is run on a second print (this test may crack it)

title: US fit on P1 with the bag: clevis bolt heads and clevis face vs the bag at every crown kit end (+ CLEVIS-FACE wear inspection); US straps on their lanes; US2 eye over the clevis seam
defined_in: designs/pack_5200/analysis/h1_bedfit.md 7 (ASSUMPTIONS HEAD-PROUD, SEAM-FLOOR); designs/pack_5200/analysis/corrie_f_body.md 25-26 (BL-050 B: us_route.head_clearance; BL-052); designs/pack_5200/analysis/h1_crown.md 3a, 7 (ASSUMPTION CLEVIS-FACE)
what_it_proves: the 4 US2 clevis bolt heads (BL-051: sunk in counterbores, x +/-179.0-182.5, 0.5 mm below the clevis outer face, z 134.0 / 150.0) do not rub the bag (free drapes: worst -1.7 mm, 15 in fill L; within 0 mm at 15 in fill L, 15 in meat L, 19 in meat L, 23 in meat L), and the bag side panel resting on the clevis's flat outer face (x +/-183.0, z 127-157; the free drapes pass 4.0 mm inside it on every drape) does not wear (CLEVIS-FACE)
gates: bag first article (BAG-BATCH): a FAIL means a frame-side head change (counterbore or cap, owner decision) before more bags
safety_at_stake: bag abrasion at the B-01 | B-03 corner over a Ti socket head under load; US strap route
specimen: P1 frame with both US2 clevises bolted on (as built), the first sewn bag, US1 / US2 straps rigged (bag on), crown kits S, M, L
steps: (1) colour each clevis bolt head AND each clevis outer face (x +/-183, z 127-157) with lipstick or chalk paste, a different colour on the face; (2) mount the bag; 30 kg sand meat on IM1-IM3, cinch the US straps; set the crown to 15 in (kit S shortest), run the T5 crank 200 cycles (or walk 5 min if T1-T4 have passed); (3) take the bag off and look for colour on B-01, B-03 and the B-18 / floor corner; photo; (4) repeat at 19 in and 23 in (kits M, L); (5) bag-off cradle: rig the US straps round a 20 kg sand bag as a quarter, check the US2 strap and its tail clear the heads; (6) slide the US2 eye across the clevis seam in the throat floor under load (SEAM-FLOOR); (7) CLEVIS-FACE INSPECTION (BL-052, ASSUMPTION CLEVIS-FACE), after step 4 and again after the T9 / T9-R3a walk on the same bag: bag off, lay it flat, find the face-colour patch on B-03 / the B-01 | B-03 corner (frame z 127-157 = about 92-122 mm above the floor seam, at the side seam), look at it under the 10x loupe against an unworn spot of the same panel: fuzz, pilled or broken face yarns, shine, coating worn through (hold to a light: pin-holes); photo both sides; record; IN THE SAME LOOK (review 5 m-9 / M-6): the US2 strap where it passes the clevis block's lower aft edge and the US1 strap where it leaves the US1 fairlead floor's lower end: fuzz, whitening or glazing on the strap, and whitening or a worn edge on the print; photo; (8) US STRAP CLEARANCE ON THE REAL BAG (BL-054, review 5 m-5: the HE-FIT bench check sets the dowel under its pin, so it cannot show the bag pulling the strap sideways): bag ON, 30 kg sand meat on IM1-IM3, both US cams cinched tight as the user card says; at 15, 19 and 23 in (kits S, M, L) slide a 10 mm (0.39 in) feeler block between each US strap and the hinge fairlead cheeks and between each US strap and the HE (eye, legs, box), both sides, along the whole strap run you can reach; record the smallest gap per strap per setting
pass_fail: no colour from the HEADS on the bag at any crown setting; (8) the 10 mm feeler passes between every US strap and the hinge cheeks / HE at S, M and L, both sides (a gap under 10 mm or contact = FAIL, photo to the pack-designer); the strap and its tail clear the heads in the cradle; the US2 eye slides across the seam without catching; CLEVIS-FACE: face colour on the panel is expected, but no fuzz, pilling, broken yarn, shine or pin-hole there after the crank cycles and after the T9 walk; FAIL: photo to the pack-designer (panel let out about 7 mm over that band, or a wear patch) and the structural-fea-engineer
cost_basis: lipstick / chalk paste; P1, bag and sand from kits C / D
notes: BL-050 B (orchestrator): new. Run with T9-R3a on P1 / the first sewn bag. BL-052: heads counterbored (BL-051), the clevis face colour and the CLEVIS-FACE wear inspection (step 7) added. BL-054 (review 5 m-5 / m-9): step 8 (US strap clearance on the real bag, every kit) and the strap / lip look in step 7

title: MT-1 cradle pull on P1: cradle belly set by the user card (60 mm minimum, strap gauge) and US1 / US2 arm-root strain at 240 / 480 / 720 N per pin
defined_in: designs/pack_5200/analysis/h1_crown.md 4 and 7 (ASSUMPTIONS BELLY-MIN, US1-STUB-GOVERNS, CROWN-SECTION); designs/pack_5200/analysis/corrie_f_body.md 26 (BL-052: BELLY-GAUGE)
what_it_proves: a hunter following the card leaves a belly >= 60 mm (US1 root fatigue 1.03 at 60 mm, 0.95 at 50 mm; h1_crown.json belly_sweep) and the US1 / US2 arm-root stress at the cradle pin loads is no more than the lug model's
gates: frame release R1 (US1 arm root: stub model 0.95 at a 50 mm belly) and the user card's belly rule
safety_at_stake: US1 arm root fatigue 1.09 at the 70 mm design belly, 1.03 at 60, 0.95 at 50 (h1_crown.md 4)
specimen: P1 frame (the sacrificial frame) on the kit C stand, bag OFF, both US2 clevises bolted on as built, the US1 / US2 straps with their sewn gauge tacks and USA anchors; strain gauges (1 mm foil, 120 ohm, cyanoacrylate on the sanded PAHT) on the US1 and US2 arm roots (R side, bag face, 3 mm off the stay surface, gauge axis along the arm); root stress = strain x 3.86 GPa (youngs_modulus_xy_mpa, record pa12_cf_fdm_paht); TEMPERATURE (BL-054, review 5 m-8): wire each gauge as a HALF bridge with a dummy gauge of the same lot bonded on an unloaded offcut of the same print, lying beside the specimen (it cancels the PAHT-CF's thermal strain); write the room temperature at every reading; with no dummy, re-zero the bridge unloaded at every stop and log the temperature
steps: (A) BELLY: rig the bag-off cradle round a 20 kg sand bag as a quarter; a helper who has not read this sheet cams the US1 and US2 straps following the packaging card only (3 tries, re-rigged each time); lay a straight stick across each strap's two pins and measure the strap's drop at mid-span with a rule; record 3 x 2 bellies and the gauge readings; (B) PIN PULLS: per strap, eye on its pin, the strap led along its lane leg (45 deg below the pin line for US1, 23 deg for US2, the 70 mm design belly; h1_crown.json belly_sweep) to a turnbuckle and the crane scale anchored to the stand; zero the gauges; pull to 240 / 480 / 720 N (24.5 / 48.9 / 73.4 kg), hold 10 s at each, read both gauges; unload, read the zero again; loupe on both arm roots
pass_fail: (A) every measured belly >= 60 mm (6 of 6); (B) measured root stress at each step <= the h1_crown lug model's root stress at that load (the structural-fea-engineer reads it off), zero returns within 5 % of the 720 N reading, no crack or whitening at either root
cost_basis: strain gauges and bridge parts on the shopping list (kit B); P1, stand and sand from kits C / A
notes: BL-052: new. The 'MT-1 cradle pull' of h1_crown.md (the register's MT-1 is the bench box-X proof). Run on P1 before T1 on P2, so a root that reads above the model stops the carry tests
